studies.summary: The primary abstract reports bacterial carriage during amoeba spore dispersal with benefits conditional on food availability at the destination.
studies.caveat: Publisher access exposed the abstract and figure titles, not the complete article or methods. Later causal studies revise a host-only interpretation; this record remains E1.

studies.summary: Symbiont acquisition and removal change food-carriage phenotypes; carriage persists through four subsequent social cycles without fresh symbiont addition, with conditional reproductive benefits.
studies.caveat: Transfers use pooled spores and renewed food bacteria, allowing mixed transmission and reacquisition. Stock history overlaps the earlier research program; single-spore inheritance is not guaranteed.

studies.summary: Food carriage is predominantly extracellular; downstream fruiting after transfer depends on symbiont identity and dispersal geometry, and carriage does not uniformly improve host reproduction.
studies.caveat: All experiments use one host clone, with repeated assays nested within it. Transferred sori are mixed propagules; conditional plot denominators and host costs prevent equating bacterial presence with reproductive success.

independence.program: Connected amoeba farming research program; publications are not independent origins.
independence.2015: Multiple host clones and bacterial isolates; stock collections overlap preceding studies.
independence.2019: One host clone; multiple bacterial strains and nested assays.
independence.negative_comparator: Giger 2024 previously reviewed, distinct fungal system and imposed pairing; not a matched comparison or new record.
